literal sites while declaring its own token set and using none of it. WAVE 3m migrated all of them.

**1. THE TOKEN SET WAS COMPLETED FIRST.** `src/next/next.css` gained the ladder steps the console actually used and
its own rules did not cover — `text-secondary` (#3f3f46) · `text-ink-900` (#18181b) · `text-ink-800` (#27272a) ·
`text-quiet` (#a1a1aa) · `text-quieter` (#d4d4d8) · `text-on-dark` (#ffffff) · `bg-tint-strong` (#e4e4e7) ·
`bg-ink-800/900/950` · `bg-scrim-30` · `bg-canvas-40…80` · `bg-tint-70/80` · `border-hairline-soft/bold` ·
`border-ink` · `border-ink-strong`. **Every value is EXACTLY what the class it replaces already compiled to**, so the
rewrite is colour-neutral by construction. The nine pre-existing rules were also given their `was <class>` record, so
the mapping is complete and machine-readable.

**2. ALL 2,025 SITES WERE REPOINTED ACROSS 44 FILES** (191 in the shared primitives and the shell that frames every
console screen; 1,555 across the screens). Evidence: the console measures **grey 1746 → 0** and **literal 279 → 0**;
`e2e/next-console-smoke.spec.ts` **6 passed** — every console screen still renders; `npm run build` **EXIT 0**;
typecheck **0 errors**.

**3. A NEW GATE MAKES IT PERMANENT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS** — `scripts/validate-next-console-tokens.mjs` (9 assertions,
auto-discovered by `validate:all`):
- **the absence guard**: the console's code authors **zero** grey-family and **zero** literal sites, measured with the
  project's OWN family regexes (imported from `measure-legacy-classes.mjs`, so there is no second definition);
- **the dead-class guard**: every console token the code uses is DECLARED in `next.css` — the defect this project has
  already paid for once, when `text-strong` emitted no rule across 97 files while every check passed;
- **the positive control**: the migration is real, discovered from `next.css`'s own `was` record (30 of 30 tokens
  used, none speculative, no replaced class still authored).
**Proved able to fail**: three raw grey classes reintroduced → **A1 FAIL** → restored byte-identical `7b62a4e9…`.

**4. THE MIGRATION NOW HAS ONE FAILING ASSERTION, AND IT IS THE METRIC'S OWN DEFECT.** `scripts/validate-legacy-styling-migration.mjs`
went **3 of 14 → 1 of 14**: only T3's ink arm remains (measured **912** against a ceiling of **468**), because the

migration repoints ONTO**. Migrating the console therefore moved its own surface names INTO the family — ink
483 → 912 — while grey fell to its ceiling and literal to zero. **This is now the single decision standing between
the project and a green migration gate**, and it cannot be fixed by migrating anything: either redefine `ink` to the
legacy aliases only (`ink*` · `brass*` — **14 sites in 2 files** today, so the arm would pass at once), or keep the
family and re-state the ceiling with the reason. Recorded in the spec §12 and left to the Owner, exactly as the
project's own §FINDING requires.

measurements above · full measurement recorded in `docs/OPENSHIP_REFERENCE_SPEC.md` §12

## §BATCH 4a — THE FOUNDATION DEFECT UNDER THE WHOLE REDESIGN: `text-strong` WAS A DEAD CLASS IN 97 FILES (2026-11-21)

**Status: FIXED at source, with a gate. Commit `a424ed8`.**

1. **WHAT WAS WRONG.** The legacy-styling migration (OpenShip Batch 10) repointed 1,663 literal
   `white`/`black` sites onto the theme's text ladder and named its target **`text-strong`**. That name was
   **never declared** in `tailwind.config.js`, so Tailwind emitted **no rule for it**. Measured before the fix:
   `resolveConfig(...).theme.colors.strong` was `undefined`, and the built stylesheet contained
   `.text-[var(--mr-text-strong)]` but **no `.text-strong`**. It was a **dead class in 97 files**.
2. **WHY IT MATTERED, MEASURABLY.** `--mr-text` is `#E8E8E8` (dark) / `#333333` (light) while
   `--mr-text-strong` is `#FFFFFF` / `#000000`. So "strong" text was **not strong on either appearance** — it
   silently inherited its parent's colour. Nothing could catch it: a class that emits no CSS cannot fail
   typecheck, the build, 198 validators, or any browser test.
3. **FIXED AT SOURCE (rule 07).** The whole text ladder the tokens already define is now declared
   (`strong` · `faint` · `soft` · `active`), plus the missing `surface.tint` key — which also made
   **`bg-surface-tint` a dead class in 3 files** (`TourEngine`, `OnboardingWizard`, `ui.tsx`), including the
   guided-tour panel's own fill.
4. **A SECOND REAL DEFECT, FOUND BY THE NEW GATE.** `NotificationCenter.tsx` used **`state-critical`** (bare)
   in 4 places, but the declared state key is **`danger`** — so the notification tone lost its colour.
   Repointed to `state-danger`; the auto-generated alpha shims were regenerated to match (1 insertion,
   3 deletions).
5. **NEW GATE (rule 07 §4) — `scripts/validate-theme-classes-resolve.mjs`.** It discovers the token vocabulary
   from its OWNER (`src/config/themes.ts`, never a retyped list), loads the Tailwind config through
   `resolveConfig`, and **FAILS** if any colour-family class the source uses does not resolve to a colour. It
   **FAILS LOUDLY when the discovery returns nothing** (rule 10 §5), and it is auto-discovered by
   `validate:all` (rule 09 §4).
6. **PROVED ABLE TO FAIL.** `strong` was removed from the config → the gate **FAILED**, naming
   `"text-strong" (97 file(s))` → the file was restored **byte-identical** (sha256 `cf37e11d…` before and
   after) → the gate **PASSED**.
7. **EVIDENCE.** `validate:all` **199 PASS / 0 FAIL** (199, not 198 — the new gate is auto-discovered) ·
   typecheck **0** · build **EXIT 0** · `theme-visual` + `accessibility` **25 passed** (axe: **0 violations**) ·
   `app-shell` + `brand-advertising` **31 passed**.

**WHY THIS BELONGS IN BATCH 4.** Batch 4 restyles the advertising screens onto this very ladder. Fixing the
ladder FIRST means Batch 4 — and Batches 5–7 — are built on a foundation that actually renders, instead of
propagating a class that does nothing.

## §BATCH 5a — THE SHARED PRIMITIVES ONTO THE CANONICAL THEME LADDER (2026-11-21)

**Status: DONE and verified in a real browser. Commit `0e78820`.**

1. **WHAT THE BATCH WAS.** The pieces EVERY signed-in screen is built from:
   `src/components/ui.tsx` (the UI kit, 23 exports), `src/components/shared/workspace.tsx`
   (frame/header/metric/queue/context primitives), `DataTable`, `dashboard`, the chart
   system, `ThemeSelector`, and the six `src/components/layout/` files (the shells, the

   everything composes; 5b = the remaining shared components.**
2. **WHAT CHANGED — COLOUR ONLY.** Legacy grey → the declared text ladder (`text-strong` ·
   `text-muted` · `text-faint`) and the surface ladder; legacy ink → the surface ladder
   (the token has always been `--mr-surface*`); `brass-*` → **`accent-*`**, the CANONICAL
   name for `--mr-accent` (declared in `tailwind.config.js` this batch as an EXACT MIRROR
   of `brass` — same tokens, so the rename moves no pixel; `VAR_BY_KEY` already carried
   `accent`); and the legacy Tailwind palette → the canonical state tones.
3. **REAL DEFECT 1 — THE ACCENT BUTTON'S LABEL WAS LIGHT-ON-ORANGE IN THE LIGHT
   APPEARANCE.** The `accent` variant used `text-ink`, which resolves to `--mr-surface` —
   dark in the dark appearance but **LIGHT in the light one**, where the project's own
   config records that white on `#FF6A00` measures only **2.34:1**. Repointed to
   `text-on-accent` (`--mr-on-accent` is **BLACK in both appearances** — verified in both
   theme blocks: `themes.ts` lines 190 and 315).

## §CLICKUP — CONNECTED AND VERIFIED LIVE (2026-11-19)

**GOVERNANCE/TOOLING increment: NO application runtime change**, so the three-way deployment
contract does not apply and the resume block above is deliberately unchanged.

### STATUS: the connection WORKS
`node scripts/clickup/auth.mjs --status` reports `configured: YES — a personal credential is
stored` and `live check: OK — workspace "Mercenta Partners's Workspace" is reachable`.

### Why a credential was needed at all
The ClickUp MCP connection on this machine **cannot** authenticate the reporting scripts: its
cached token is issued for `mcp.clickup.com`, and `api.clickup.com` rejects it with **HTTP 401
`{"err":"Oauth token not found","ECODE":"OAUTH_019"}`** (live-tested 2026-11-19).

### Which credential is in use, and why the two are kept apart
**The PERSONAL API TOKEN is the credential in use.** ClickUp's own documentation says to use a
personal token for *"individual or testing purposes"* and reserves the OAuth flow for *"apps or
integrations that other people use"* — Mercenta's scripts read one workspace, so the personal
token is the documented choice, and it never expires. **The OAuth app is registered and that
path is kept working, but its credentials are never mixed with the personal token.** The file
records which is stored: `CLICKUP_TOKEN_KIND=personal|oauth`.

### A header difference that would have caused a false failure
ClickUp accepts **two token shapes with DIFFERENT headers**: a personal token (`pk_...`) goes in
**raw**, an OAuth access token goes as a **Bearer**. The helper used to send `Bearer` for both,
which would have reported a perfectly good personal token as broken. `authHeaderFor()` now
detects the shape, and `verifyToken()` falls back to the other form before calling a token bad.
(`report.mjs` already sent the raw token, which is correct for a personal token.)


### What was built
- `scripts/clickup/auth.mjs` — a local setup page bound to **127.0.0.1 ONLY**. It offers BOTH a
  personal API token (**Option 1**, recommended) and the OAuth app flow (**Option 2**). A
  submitted token arrives in a **POST body** — never a URL, never logged, never echoed — and is
  **checked against ClickUp BEFORE it is saved**, so a rejected or wrong-workspace token is never
  written to disk. On success the server shuts itself down. The credential is stored OUTSIDE the
  project at mode 600 in a 700 directory, under the SAME key `report.mjs` already reads.
- `scripts/clickup/auth.test.mjs` — **95 offline checks, 0 failed** (was 65). No network, no real
  credential, temporary directory only.
- `scripts/clickup/report.mjs` — behaviour unchanged: 4 modes, **SELF_TEST_PASS (9 checks)**.

### Two real defects found and FIXED AT SOURCE
1. **The app-registration link pointed at a page that has no Create control.**
   `app.clickup.com/settings/apps` ("App Settings") offers only personal API tokens and authorized
   apps. The control — labelled **"Create"**, NOT "Create new app" — is on the **"ClickUp API
   Settings"** sub-tab of `app.clickup.com/{ws}/settings/team/{ws}/clickup-api/settings`.
   **ClickUp's own documentation is out of date here**, and the helper had been sending the Owner
   to the wrong page. `APPS_PAGE` is §REPOINTED, and the test that required the old URL is
   §REPOINTED too — repointed, never weakened.
2. **The credential page was CACHEABLE**, so after the helper changed the browser kept serving the
   OLD single-option form (a stale credential page — unsafe as well as confusing). Every html
   response now carries `Cache-Control: no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate`.

## §INTEGRATION LAYER — BUILT AND RUNNING IN THE CLOUD (2026-11-19)

**GOVERNANCE/TOOLING increment: NO application runtime change.** Adds `scripts/integration/` and
`.github/workflows/integration.yml`.

### What it does
A **READ-ONLY** reconciliation and reporting layer across four systems. It reads, diffs against
recorded fingerprints, records a redacted audit trail, and reports. **It writes to no system**, so
there is no uncontrolled bidirectional overwrite — and no claim of one.

| Property | Where it lives |
|---|---|
| Incremental sync | only fingerprints that CHANGED are reported as changes |
| Idempotency | every item keyed; a repeat run reports **zero** changes (proven live) |
| Retry / recovery | `lib/core.mjs request()` retries 429/5xx/network with jittered backoff |
| Rate-limit awareness | `Retry-After` honoured; ClickUp lists walked sequentially |
| Conflict detection | duplicate refs, ClickUp status regressions, workflow regressions |
| Audit trail | `appendAudit()`, one REDACTED JSONL record per action |
| Cached state | `reports/integration/state.json` (gitignored), persisted in CI by `actions/cache` |
| Health monitoring | `check()` per system, reported centrally |

### Google Drive — no new dependency
The existing service-account key carries `client_email` + `private_key` + `token_uri`, so Google's
**JWT-bearer flow is implemented with `node:crypto`**. Scope is **`drive.readonly` ONLY**; a test
asserts the connector contains no PUT/PATCH/DELETE and no write endpoint.

### Cloud automation — the Mac can be off
`.github/workflows/integration.yml` runs on a GitHub runner: **daily 05:00 UTC**, **weekly Monday
06:00 UTC**, plus `workflow_dispatch`. `permissions: contents: read` — it cannot push or deploy.
Four **encrypted repository secrets** were set from the protected local files over stdin; the
values were never printed, never in argv, and remain non-retrievable.

### Verified live
- Local: all four HEALTHY · first run 53 ClickUp + 30 GitHub + 9 Drive added ·
  **second run 0 added / 0 changed / 53 + 30 unchanged** (idempotency) · 0 secret leaks
- **Cloud run `44551199355`: `conclusion=success`, job ✓ in 47s**, artifact published —
  clickup **53** · github **20** · penpot **yes (0)** · drive **9 files** · all four HEALTHY
- `INTEGRATION_SELF_TEST_PASS (90 checks, 0 failed)`, proved able to fail by two mutations
- `FULL VALIDATOR CORPUS: 197 PASS / 0 FAIL` — baseline preserved

### Four real defects found by running it, fixed at source
1. `nowIso` used but never imported in `sync.mjs` — the CLI crashed on its first live run.
2. `github.snapshot` returned `ok:true` when **every** request failed — an unreachable GitHub would
   have been reported healthy. It now fails when nothing could be read.
3. The sync layer passed an **ENV object where a timestamp belonged**, making the Drive JWT's
   `iat`/`exp` NaN so every token request failed. Non-finite clocks now fall back; Drive then found
   all 9 files.
4. The CLI entry guard used `new URL(import.meta.url).pathname`, which **percent-encodes** this
   project's path (`1. Mercenta` → `1.%20Mercenta`) — the same class already documented in
   `report.mjs`. The CLI exited 0 having done nothing. Now `fileURLToPath`.

### Limitations, stated honestly
Read-only; **no bidirectional synchronisation**. Cross-system semantic conflicts need an explicit
object link, which does not exist. Penpot design references need a file connected via **MCP →
Connect**. Drive is discovery only. The **ten Dependabot PRs were untouched**.

### Remaining owner actions
1. Connect a Penpot design file (**MCP → Connect**) for design references.
2. The **`schedule:` trigger fires only on the DEFAULT branch (`main`)**. The workflow is verified
   working on `redesign/foundation` via `workflow_dispatch`; for it to run automatically it must
   reach `main`. Adding one file to the default branch is the owner's call.

Root cause, established by isolation rather than guesswork: `tailwind.config.js` declared the scale as a NESTED object (`borderRadius` with an inner `ds` object), and **Tailwind 3.4 silently emits NO utility for a nested scale object** — a minimal config with the same shape produced no rule, while the same config with FLAT keys produced `border-radius: 16px`. Measured in the built stylesheet: **zero** occurrences of the class, against **195 + 431 + 88 = 714 class sites** in the source. It had been inert since §PHASE C4 and through BATCH 3 and BATCH 4, and nothing caught it because every check read the config BLOCK or the source — none read the CSS Tailwind actually generates. The keys are now FLAT (same class names, so no call site moved), and the gate COMPILES the config in memory and fails if the three used steps do not really emit their value.

## PREVIOUS PLATFORM POSITION — **§PHASE C4: THE RADIUS + ELEVATION SCALE — THE APP NOW HAS ONE, AND THE 642 CLASS SITES THAT HAD NO PLACE IN ONE ARE GONE** (session 139, 2026-10-13)

1. **COMPLETED / VERIFIED — ONE RADIUS SCALE, DECLARED ONCE.** `tailwind.config.js` now declares `borderRadius.ds` = `sm` 6px (inline: chips, tags, `kbd`/`<code>`, thumbnails, micro icon buttons) · `md` 8px (controls: buttons, inputs, selects, textareas, tabs, nav items) · `lg` 12px (containers: cards, panels, modals, popovers, tables) · `pill` 9999px, with a 16px step permitted ONLY on large marketing/hero blocks (`src/components/marketing/`) and Tailwind's own pill step accepted as an alias for the pill role. The measurement that forced it: the product rendered **630 class sites with no place in any named step** (`rounded-lg` 387 · `rounded-md` 97 · bare `rounded` 85 · `rounded-xl` 58 · `rounded-full` 76 · `rounded-2xl` 4 · `rounded-sm` 3) while the named steps were consumed almost nowhere (41 · 26 · 22). **The two named steps were moved ONTO the geometry the app already rendered** — the control step 10px → 8px, the container step 14px → 12px — which is what makes this a RENAME rather than a redesign: binding `rounded-lg` → `ds-md` and `rounded-xl` → `ds-lg` moves NO pixels for 542 sites, and only 41 + 26 occurrences moved by 2px. 4px (bare `rounded`) was folded into 6px, because a 2px difference between two small steps is not a step, it is noise — and it was used inconsistently on chips and `<code>`.
2. **COMPLETED / VERIFIED — ONE ELEVATION SCALE, AND THE 19 UNNAMED SHADOWS ARE ON IT.** The four roles were already theme-driven in `src/config/themes.ts` (`--mr-shadow-subtle` resting · `--mr-shadow-raised` interactive · `--mr-shadow-overlay` floating, plus `shadow-ds-none` for a control that must sit flat); 19 unnamed shadows sat beside them, **15 of those `shadow-2xl` on exactly the surfaces OVERLAY exists for** (modals, popovers, dropdowns, floating cards), plus one hover lift, one active pill, one link button and one brass glow. All 19 are now on the role that matches what they are, and one behaviour note is stated rather than hidden: on the active onboarding step the old `shadow-lg` + brass glow becomes a neutral `shadow-ds-raised`, because a token shadow bakes its colour into the variable, so the colour utility would have become dead weight — it was removed rather than left pretending to work. An INSET glow is not elevation and was not migrated: `shadow-[inset_…]` in `src/components/marketing/Home.tsx` is a decorative inner-stamp effect, and the gate permits an arbitrary shadow ONLY when it is inset, so an outer one can never hide behind that allowance.
3. **COMPLETED / VERIFIED — FIVE REAL DEFECTS FIXED AT SOURCE (rule 07), NOT REPORTED.** (1) `src/index.css` `:focus-visible` forced `border-radius: 4px`: focusing ANY control visibly snapped its corners to a radius the ramp does not declare. Removed — an `outline` already follows the element's own radius. (2) `[data-record-focused='true']` forced `6px` for the same reason — removed. (3) The scrollbar thumb used a 4px radius on an 8px-wide thumb, i.e. half its width: the intent was a pill, now expressed as the pill step (pixel-identical). (4) `ds-focus` and `ds-focus-danger` were DECLARED in `tailwind.config.js` and consumed NOWHERE, while `docs/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` claimed "focus rings `shadow-ds-focus`" — a live claim that was false. The tokens were REMOVED and the claim corrected; the focus mechanism is the canonical `:focus-visible` outline. (5) `Modal` sat on the CONTROL step while `Card` sat on the CONTAINER step, although a dialog is a container and every other overlay in the app was already 12px — moved onto the container step.
4. **COMPLETED / VERIFIED — THE GATE (rule 10 §4/§5/§6, DISCOVERED and mutation-proved).** `scripts/validate-radius-elevation-scale.mjs` — **42 assertions**, wired automatically into `npm run validate:all` (which globs `scripts/validate-*.mjs`, so a new gate cannot be forgotten). It does NOT retype the ramp: it DISCOVERS it from `tailwind.config.js` (the owner) and **fails loudly when a discovery comes back empty**. It fails on a reappearing unnamed radius (including **per-side** forms such as `rounded-t-lg` and arbitrary radius values), on `rounded-2xl` escaping the marketing folder, on a reappearing unnamed OUTER shadow, on a declared token with no consumer (the absence guard that caught the dead focus tokens), on a theme missing an elevation role, on a `border-radius` literal in CSS outside the ramp, on a live describer stating an undeclared size, and on either program keeping its own copy of the class-list test.
5. **COMPLETED / VERIFIED — THE MIGRATION IS MECHANICAL AND IDEMPOTENT.** `scripts/migrate-radius-elevation.mjs` (`npm run migrate:radius-elevation`) makes the token first and the change mechanical: 619 replacements across 107 files, then 2 blind-spot sites, then 1 per-side site — and a re-run reports **0 changes** (proven). It rewrites ONLY real class lists, never comments and never prose, which matters because this project RECORDS its changes in comments that quote class names.
6. **COMPLETED / VERIFIED — THREE BLIND SPOTS FOUND BY THE TOOLS THEMSELVES AND CLOSED.** (a) The first migration rule could not see a **per-side** `rounded-t-lg` (one live site); found by the gate's per-side check, then fixed in the migration too. (b) The first scanner read backtick-quoted class names INSIDE the project's own §PHASE comments as code and reported 2 false offenders in `src/components/ui.tsx` — a gate punishing the documentation the rules require — so the class-list test now lives in ONE module, `scripts/lib/design-scale-scan.mjs`, imported by BOTH the migration and the gate so they cannot drift. (c) **The negative test found a real hole in the gate itself:** the theme check counted substrings, so a theme that had LOST an elevation role still passed, because the renamed declaration `'--mr-shadow-raised-OLD':` contains the old name. It now matches the declaration itself.
7. **REMAINING — CURRENT ROADMAP.** C4's leftovers are Radix for `Modal`/`Select`/`Tabs` (only where it materially improves keyboard/ARIA behaviour, each package and reason recorded) and CVA variants behind the EXISTING props. Then **D** the application-wide premium rollout (the 24 recorded hand-rolled tables, the 3,137 hardcoded dark classes, then the `src/index.css` force-patch removal with an absence guard proved able to fail), **E** the deterministic investor demonstration, **F** per-provider setup completeness and **G** the acceptance/regression pass.
8. **CURRENT CHECKPOINT / VERIFICATION STATUS** — `typecheck` **0** (four projects) · `lint` **0** · `build` **ok** · `validate:all` **193 PASS / 0 FAIL** (192 + the new gate) · `validate:radius-elevation` **42/42** · `validate-registry-integrity` **7 PASS / 0 FAIL** · `validate-no-stale-blockers` **58/58** · `validate-resume-state` **PASS** · `validate-e6-brand-surfaces` **PASS** (the rename's 118-file surface is DECLARED, exact paths only, in `PHASE_C4_DESIGN_SCALE_SCOPE`) · `e2e/theme-visual` + `e2e/typography-scale` + `e2e/crm` + `e2e/onboarding` **28 passed** · the 30 rendered theme baselines compared **BEFORE/AFTER**: all 30 changed, **median 0.041% of pixels, maximum 0.397%** · **NEGATIVE TEST: 7 independent mutations, each failed the gate, every file restored byte-identical** (sha256 recorded) · `git status --porcelain` EMPTY at the recorded checkpoint.

brand does not. The marketplace is the **UK** (`A1F83G8C2ARO7P`). The ten approved categories are the Amazon
UK Vendor Central categories, declared ONCE in `src/types.ts` (`APPROVED_CATEGORIES`).

**Do NOT ask the Founder to confirm the channel, the marketplace, or whether another channel should be
considered. Never raise "which marketplace" or "should we start the Amazon process" as an open question — it
is NOT open. It is already decided and already recorded.**

Canonical sources (READ these; do not re-derive, do not ask):
`.clinerules/mercenta-business-model.md` · `docs/MERCENTA_BUSINESS_MODEL.md` §1 ·
`src/lib/spapi/transform.ts → UK_MARKETPLACE_ID` · `src/types.ts → APPROVED_CATEGORIES`.

## INTEGRATIONS — THE REQUIRED SHAPE IS ONE-CLICK CONNECT (Founder directive 2026-09-27)

**Every third-party provider must be connected by the operator in ONE action from its card in Integration
Settings: click Connect → the wizard either asks for the API key or sends the operator to the provider's own
login → a "Test connection" step runs → the card shows the real result. Nothing else may ever be required of
the operator, and entering a real key must never require a code change.**

**What EXISTS TODAY (verified in the code — `src/components/admin/integrations/IntegrationsPanel.tsx`,
`src/integrations/registry.ts`, `src/integrations/IntegrationsContext.tsx`, `src/integrations/types.ts`):** the
Connect button; the generic `ConnectWizard` (provider choice → credential input → Test connection → done); the
per-card health check; Live / Configuring / "(Mock)" status; and ONE registry that drives the wizard for every
provider, so a provider change is data, not a new screen.

**What is MISSING — the backend half, and it is the same missing plumbing recorded elsewhere:** steps 2–3 of
the wizard (secure key exchange + encrypted secret storage, and the real harmless test call) are NOT wired.
Today a connect completes flagged `sandbox: true` and is labelled "(Mock)". Secrets currently sit in the
browser for the demo; real secrets must live in a vault — and **the connection-record vault schema does not exist
yet**: `supabase/migrations/0002_integration_connections.sql` is named in this file's older text but is NOT in the
repository (27 migrations, none for integration connections), so writing it is Batch 1b work. A real key must never
be left in localStorage or a plain column.

**Safety rule that must NOT be relaxed:** a simulated connect must never be shown or treated as live. In demo
mode the click works and is honestly marked simulated; with a real key the SAME wizard path performs the real
exchange + test and flips to Live — no code change.

  for "parity"; parking a fixable defect in a "known exceptions" / "recorded for later" list; reporting a defect
  instead of fixing it; and omitting a fix to keep a report short or to avoid extending a declared scope. Every fix

  byte-identical). The ONLY alternative is **BLOCKED**, which must name the exact missing input/authority, the exact
  next action, and must never describe the affected behaviour as working. A session report may therefore use only
  **FIXED (with evidence)** or **BLOCKED (with the missing input)** — "recorded" is not a disposition. The global
  `reference-implementation-parity-check.md` was extended in the same pass with the matching exception ("parity with a
  known defect is a defect, not parity"), so the two rules cannot be read as contradictory.

## PREVIOUS POSITION — **BATCH 1c (S6): THE ENFORCEMENT LEG NOW EXISTS — CI runs every gate on every push and pull request, and a gate keeps that wiring honest** (2026-09-28, session 42) — HISTORICAL

**Why this was the next task:** every recorded gate (`typecheck`, `lint`, `build`, the whole validator corpus)
depended on a person remembering to run it. `.github/` held **only `dependabot.yml`**. So a break could be
committed and pushed unseen — and one already had: the registry row `batch-4-ci-cd` cited
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` as its evidence **while no such file existed anywhere in the repository**. A capability
that is claimed and absent is a defect, not a gap.

**What now exists (verified this session):**

- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — on **every push and every pull request**: `npm ci` (reproducible, from the
  committed lockfile — never `npm install`) → `typecheck` → `lint` → `build` → **`validate:wording`** →
  **`validate:all`** (the whole corpus, **116 validators**, globbed by `scripts/validate-all.sh`). It installs
  the Chromium the production-boot gate drives, cancels superseded runs, is time-bounded (`timeout-minutes`),
  holds `contents: read` only, pins `actions/checkout@v4` / `actions/setup-node@v4` with Node 20 + the npm cache,
  interpolates **no secret**, and contains **no deploy command**.
- **`scripts/validate-ci-wiring.mjs`** — `npm run validate:ci-wiring`, **43 assertions**. It refuses a workflow
  that is missing, untriggered on push or PR, unpinned, non-failing (`continue-on-error`), disabled
  (`if: false`), wrongly ordered (build must precede `validate:all`), secret-bearing, deploy-bearing, or that
  names a gate whose script/config does not exist; and it asserts — mechanically — that **every registered
  `validate:*` script is reachable by CI**, inside the corpus glob or named explicitly by the workflow.
- **The wording gate is named explicitly** because `scripts/validate-all.sh` globs `scripts/validate-*.mjs` and
  the compliance wording gate is `scripts/lint-wording.mjs` — a name that glob cannot match. That coverage gap is
  closed by an explicit CI step and asserted, rather than left to trust.

a workflow file that did not exist and described gates it did not run → the file now exists and the row states

**Why this was the next task:** Batch 1a made the provider *proxy* helpers real, but the Founder's goal — *"when I get
the API keys, I should just need to give them to you and everything will sync up"* — still failed at the very first
step. The wizard's "Test Connection & Save" pinged the provider **from the browser** and kept the key in memory only
(no storage, and for most providers no test at all), the OAuth path called
`/functions/v1/spapi-token-exchange` — **a function that did not exist** — and the connection record the live
factories read (`src/integrations/connections.ts` needs `metadata.secretRef` starting `vault:`) had **no table
behind it** (the `0002_integration_connections.sql` cited in older documents was never in the repository). So a real
key could not become a real connection.

**What now exists (verified this session):**

- **The connection-record schema — `supabase/migrations/028_create_integration_connections.sql`.** ONE record per
  provider (Mercenta's own operator accounts, not brand data): staff-only RLS, **no DELETE policy** (records are
  retained), `secret_ref` CHECK-constrained to the `vault:` scheme, and a **non-sandbox (LIVE) row MUST carry a vault
  reference** — so a "Live" record with no stored credential, or a plaintext secret in that column, cannot exist at
  the database boundary.
- **The Vault WRITE half** — `_shared/vault.ts → writeVaultSecret` + `credentialSecretName` (deterministic naming, so
  a re-connect UPDATES rather than duplicating; returns a boolean only, never the value).
- **The API-key connect path** — `_shared/providerConnect.ts` (executable handler) + `integration-connect/index.ts`.
  The harmless test runs SERVER-SIDE with the submitted key; on a genuine 2xx the credential is written to Vault and
  **only the `vault:` reference comes back**; the browser never holds a real secret.
- **The SP-API OAuth exchange** — `_shared/tokenExchange.ts` + `spapi-token-exchange/index.ts`: the real Amazon
  Login-with-Amazon code exchange, with the refresh token stored in Vault as a credential blob.
- **The wizard wiring** — `testApiKey` calls the server function (no browser ping, no client-side secret handling);
  `completeOAuthExchange` now sends the **`redirect_uri` the popup actually used**; the returned reference is stored
  on the connection; `src/lib/integrations/connectClient.ts` is the ONE place that builds an Edge-Function URL.
- **The gate** — `scripts/validate-connect-wizard-backend.mjs`, registered as `npm run validate:connect-wizard`:
  **49 assertions**, the FAKE-KEY REHEARSAL. It EXECUTES the handlers with a scripted transport and a recording Vault
  writer.

**Behaviour, stated exactly (each proven by the gate, not asserted):**

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Simulation | only when explicitly requested (`simulate: true`); **zero network calls, zero writes**, `simulated: true`, and a `mock:` reference that never starts with `vault:` |
| A **bad key** | the provider's real endpoint IS called; rejected with the provider's own error text; **nothing stored** |
| A **good key** | verified, stored in Vault; only `vault:<name>` returned — the secret is never echoed back to the caller |
| Verified but **unstorable** | reported FAILED (`VAULT_WRITE_FAILED`), never as a connection |
| A provider with **no declared test endpoint** | `TEST_ENDPOINT_NOT_DECLARED` — no endpoint is invented, nothing stored |
| A provider with **no API at all** (CSV import) | recorded via the new `markManualConnect`; **nothing live is claimed** |
| A **live** call | requires a verified operator session (`super_admin`/`admin_staff`) — a brand can never connect a provider with Mercenta's credentials |

Declared harmless test endpoints today (**7**): `openrouter`, `hunter`, `instantly`, `email/postmark`,
`email/sendgrid`, `lead_sourcing/apollo`, `lead_sourcing/instantly`. **The other 14 providers** (Stripe, E-Signature,
Amazon Ads, Keepa, Firecrawl, Usertour, Twilio WhatsApp, Postiz, Xero, Google, Wise, Payoneer, Companies House, HMRC)
have **no declared endpoint yet** and therefore refuse honestly — they are ROADMAP work, and entering a key for them
stores nothing.

**DEFECTS FOUND THIS SESSION — ALL FIXED AT SOURCE (none parked):** (1) the wizard marked CSV import `connected`
with `sandbox:false`, i.e. it displayed **"Live"** although nothing had been verified → now `markManualConnect`;
(2) registry row `stage1-token-exchange-edge-function` claimed a file that **did not exist** → the file now exists
and the row is reconciled (and deliberately `built`, not `built_and_tested`, because that enum demands an e2e
reference and none exercises this path); (3) **five validators** carried statements the new migration made false
(three pinned "the newest migration is 027" and two listed `integration_connections` among names that "DO NOT
EXIST") → every live citation repointed, with the migration now required to be **declared by the current phase** (an
undeclared new migration still fails) and the created table **pinned** as RLS-protected.

> limits): programme **§11** in `docs/DASHBOARD_LOGISTICS_CLEANUP_PROGRAMME_2026-09-22.md`.

> **The authoritative resume data is the `## CURRENT RESUME STATE` block above — read that first; it is all a new
> session needs.** This section records what P7 actually changed and how it was verified. Full detail (what was
> missing, what was built, the verification and the honest limits): `docs/DASHBOARD_LOGISTICS_CLEANUP_PROGRAMME_2026-09-22.md` **§11**.

**Increment identity (this session): P7 of the programme document (application work), programme decision 2, registers
`AV-022` / `AV-018` / `S11` / `S14`, matrix `D11-01` + the new `D11-13`.**

1. **A receipt is now a modelled concept with ONE owner.** `src/lib/commerce/receivingStatus.ts` (NEW) derives
   `not_received` / `partially_received` / `received` from the per-line received quantities (never a stored copy) and
   owns the **fail-closed "invoice only AFTER receipt" gate** (`AV-018`) — an unreceived PO cannot be invoiced, and the
   refusal names the register. A partial receipt may be invoiced, on the quantity that actually arrived.
2. **Terms are per invoice, and the due date follows the invoice.** `src/lib/commerce/invoiceTerms.ts` (NEW) owns
   **14/30/60 chosen per invoice** (decision 2) plus every figure derived from them — the derived due date, overdue,
   upcoming and **receivables = issued-and-unpaid** in ONE implementation, with the S14 basis ("no Vendor Payments API
   exists, so a payment date is derived") carried as text. This replaced SIX independent re-derivations.
3. **Invoice numbers are a registry, not a string.** `src/lib/commerce/invoiceRegistry.ts` (NEW) implements `AV-022`:
   unique + **never reused**, an append-only ledger whose VOIDED numbers stay consumed for ever, the **zero-value
   refusal**, and cancel ⇒ **NEW Invoice ID**. The first number keeps the established shape; a correction after a
   cancellation is `SIM-INV-<poNumber>-R2`, with the re-issue chain linked both ways.
4. **Cancellation is a real, attributed, audited step.** NEW `cancelCommerceInvoice` requires a STATED reason, voids
   the number for ever, and **refuses to cancel a settled invoice** — money that has moved is corrected on the ledger,
   never by rewriting an issued record.
5. **The admin surfaces.** The Retail Pipeline gains the per-PO **terms selector**, the **receiving status**, the
   invoice's own terms + derived due date, the `AV-022` rule list and the **cancel + reason** path; **Accounting** gains
   the **invoice-number registry ledger** (allocated / void / receivables / upcoming) with the basis stated.
6. **The whole thing is gated.** New `scripts/validate-p7-invoicing.mjs` (115 assertions, 0 network calls; proved able
   to fail) and `e2e/invoicing.spec.ts` (3 passed) — and the LIVE leg additionally reads the refusal codes out of the
   **deployed bundle's own chunks**, so a stale build cannot pass by looking right.

**Historical (P6 and earlier):** the headings below are the superseded position records. **The authoritative resume
data is the `CURRENT RESUME STATE` block above.**

## PREVIOUS POSITION — **P6 DONE: the PO document pack (automatic on acceptance) + the documented collect chain** (2026-09-23, session 19) — HISTORICAL

> **The authoritative resume data is the `## CURRENT RESUME STATE` block above — read that first; it is all a new
> session needs.** This section records what P6 actually changed and how it was verified; the blocks below it are
> historical.

**Increment identity (this session): P6 of `docs/DASHBOARD_LOGISTICS_CLEANUP_PROGRAMME_2026-09-22.md` (application
work), programme decisions 6/9, matrix `D10-10`.** Full detail: that document's **§10 "P6 — what was built, verified
and how"**.

1. **A document is now a first-class thing, not a button.** `src/lib/documents/poDocumentPack.ts` (NEW) owns the pack:
   **SSCC carton labels · carrier label · freight waybill · packing list/delivery note · ASN sheet · the three customs
   documents**. Each document carries `applicable` + `notApplicableReason`, `ready` + `notReadyReason`, the renderer
   that presents it and its fields — so a document that does not apply or is not yet producible is **stated**, never
   silently missing and never faked.
2. **SSCC-18 is generated, not mentioned.** `src/lib/documents/sscc.ts` (NEW) implements the published GS1 mod-10
   check digit and a **deterministic** serial from `PO number + carton index` (a reprint is byte-identical), under a
   declared **UNASSIGNED placeholder GS1 prefix** (`0000000`, `XX-PENDING-GS1-LICENCE` printed on every label).
   Replacing that one value with Mercenta's licensed prefix is the entire activation.
3. **It is automatic on acceptance.** The acceptance path (`src/lib/commerce/proxyProcessor.ts`) generates the pack in
   the same action that files the ASN, records `documentsGeneratedAt` / `documentCount` / `documentsReady` as
   **evidence only** (the pack is derived on read — no second copy to drift) and emits the canonical
   **`po_documents_ready`** event.
4. **The brand's job is now downloadable.** The Logistics Hub gains **"Documents for this PO"**
   (`src/components/shared/logistics/PoDocumentPackPanel.tsx`, NEW) with printable previews; the carrier label and the
   waybill open the **EXISTING** dialogues (one renderer per artefact, P6 did not re-implement them).
5. **The queue is visible where the work is.** The **brand** Logistics Hub nav badge and the notification centre carry
   the document-download queue from the ONE rule `documentsAwaitingDownload`. The **admin** rail deliberately has NO
   logistics badge: its destination renders `LogisticsControl`, which lists no document queue (P3's badge rule).
6. **Customs documents are lane-scoped.** They are **delegated** to the existing owner and apply to **international
   lanes only** — on a UK domestic lane they are still LISTED, with the reason.
7. **The destination is the PO's, always (P5 held).** Every document names the FC the purchase order declares; an
   undeclared PO fails closed to the explicit not-declared string, and no document ever names a Mercenta site.
8. **The collect lane shows the DOCUMENTED chain.** `src/lib/shipping/collectChain.ts` (NEW) models
   request → carrier assigned → ARN → pickup with the channel's **two-BUSINESS-day** pickup rule (register `AV-014`,
   weekend-skipping). The channel-produced steps are read **only** from
   `ChannelInstructionOutcome.routingInstructions` and report `awaiting_channel` until that record carries them —
   **an ARN cannot be fabricated by the platform** (populating it via `getShipmentDetails` is P12's scope).

**Verification (this session):** `scripts/validate-po-documents.mjs` (NEW) → **PASS (50 assertions, 0 network calls)**
and **proved able to fail** (check digit mod 10 → mod 9 → FAIL 2 of 50) · `e2e/po-documents.spec.ts` (NEW) → **6

failed / 2 skipped (16.1m)** · **demo deployed** (33/33 servable files byte-identical) and **live-verified: 44/44
checks, 0 page errors**.

## CURRENT PLATFORM POSITION — **P5 DONE: the Mercenta Hub is removed; the destination is the FC on the purchase order** (2026-09-23, session 17) — HISTORICAL

**Increment identity (this session): P5 of `docs/DASHBOARD_LOGISTICS_CLEANUP_PROGRAMME_2026-09-22.md` (application work),
plus the P4-carried copy item. Closes matrix `D09-13` and register `AV-026` / `AV-027`.**

   `ShipToParty` and `PurchaseOrder.shipToParty` — the channel's own ship-to party, whose id IS the
   fulfilment-centre code (`shipToPartyId`, register `S5`; `AV-017` records the PO as authoritative).
   `src/config/destinationFc.ts` (NEW) is its ONE owner: `resolveDestinationFc`, `fcByCode`, `destinationLabelForPo`,
   `declaredShipToParty`, `declaredDestinationLabel`.

   Mercenta-chosen site is ever substituted, and no destination is ever guessed.

   (the coordinate), the `'northampton, uk'` city point, the `resolveGeoPlace` hub branch and `MERCENTA_HUB_PLACE`
   (the Hero's hub marker) are removed. The canonical pre-live state is **`destination_fc`** — *arrival at the FC the
   PO declares* — which is what a carrier `delivered` milestone actually means.

   track (`commerceLifecycle`), the map progress (`operationsMap`), the status tones (`statusPresentation`), both
   carrier transforms (DHL, Palletline), the legacy bootstrap row, the investor-demo drill, the carrier surfaces, and
   the public lifecycle copy (FAQ + How It Works).

   hub kind is no longer drawn on the UK tile; the map draws `amazon_fc` nodes and can produce no hub node.
6. **Gates repointed, never weakened** — `validate-logistics-map` **60 → 74 assertions** (the retired hub and the
   hub's city must now fail closed; 12 new §P5 checks execute the real resolver and prove every seeded PO/shipment
   destination is its own PO's FC and that **no seeded consignment is destined for a Mercenta site**);
   `validate-logistics-hero` (54), `validate-mock-providers`, `validate-investor-demo`,
   `e2e/status-semantics`, `e2e/table-migrations`, and a NEW browser test 17 in `e2e/logistics-hub-map.spec.ts`.
   `validate-e6`/`validate-e7` had the P5 scope declared in their existing mechanism (an unexplained or protected
   change still fails).
7. **Copy pass (carried over from P4):** the admin Overview h1 no longer reads the stale "Operations Overview" — it
   reads **"Overview"**, which is the page's actual role now that Operations is a separate destination. Both browser
   assertions that named the old title were repointed with the old contract recorded inline (one of them had become
   unable to fail, and now genuinely can).

  `vendor-react` (recharts) and `vendor-other` (lodash/reselect) import **each other**, so recharts' module-level calls
  ran before their imports initialised. **Fixed** by keeping ALL of `node_modules` in ONE `vendor` chunk
  (`vite.config.ts`, full post-mortem inline). **New permanent gate: `scripts/validate-production-boot.mjs`**
  (`npm run validate:production-boot`) — it builds, serves `dist`, loads it in Chromium and asserts the app actually
  mounts; **proven to fail on the pre-fix bundle (exit 1) and pass on the fixed bundle (exit 0)**. Rebuilt, redeployed
  and **live-verified 13/13 checks on `https://demo.mercenta.co.uk`** (heading 8).

## 🧭 PREVIOUS POSITION — WAVE 4: THE BRAIN IS A GENUINE 3D SPATIAL EXPERIENCE (2026-09-22, session 9)

**Increment identity:** Wave 4 of the full UI/UX redesign. The Brain's flat 2D SVG graph is REPLACED by a real WebGL scene (perspective camera, orbit navigation, spatial cluster wheel, depth-stratified records, animated relationships, travelling signals). **The canonical Brain DATA was not touched** — `buildGraph.ts` is unchanged, the graph still owns no business state and still makes zero network calls.

**Full record:** `docs/UIUX_WAVE4_BRAIN_3D_2026-09-22.md` (reuse table with licences, the non-reuse justification, the three measured defects and their real root causes, the accessibility model, verification, and the honest gaps).

### 1. COMPLETED / VERIFIED

- **Open-source reuse, actually integrated (not cited):** `three@0.186.0` (MIT), `@react-three/fiber@8.18.0` (MIT), `@react-three/drei@9.122.0` (MIT) — R3F v8 pinned deliberately because v9 requires React 19 and this project is React 18.3. `@types/three@0.186.0` declared explicitly. **Justified non-reuse:** no open-source 3D graph library was adopted because each would have imposed a second node/edge schema over canonical contracts, replaced deterministic placement with a stochastic force simulation, and provided no accessible DOM entity layer.
- **Founder-provided skills actually used:** `emilkowalski/skills` (`pick-ui-library`, `emil-design-eng`) and `jakubkrehel/skills` (`better-ui`, `better-accessibility`) — cloned (MIT, gitignored reference material) and their concrete rules applied: instant (not smooth) mount scroll, static cue alongside every motion, `scale(0)` never used as an entrance, reduced-motion suppression, hit areas.
- **One new canonical module:** `src/lib/intelligence/brain/project.ts` — THE projection (camera definition + world→screen + DOM application), deliberately three.js-free so it can run before the first paint AND every frame. `layout3d.ts` adds the spatial projection of the existing `layout.ts` placement authority (which now also exposes `ring`/`angleDeg`), so placement still has exactly one owner.
- **Three real defects found by browser measurement and fixed at the root** (not worked around): overlapping fixed-size hit boxes (measured node spacing ≈ 11 px vs 18–56 px boxes); records outside the frustum being unreachable because the layer is clipped by the canvas box; and `visibleNodes: 0` at the instant the surface became interactive (positions only arrived on the first animation frame, worsened by an initial `React.lazy` split, which was then removed because the async gap WAS the defect).
- **Accessibility preserved and extended:** every entity is still a real, named DOM element with the same `brain-node-<id>` testid; the wrapper is `role="group"` with a counts + keyboard text alternative and now supports arrow-key record navigation, Enter/Space select and Escape clear.

## 🧭 CURRENT PLATFORM POSITION — CANONICAL PROPAGATION: BRAIN + LOGISTICS ARE NOW DYNAMIC PROJECTIONS (2026-09-21, session 6)

Branch `redesign/foundation`. **Start HEAD `22b6b62`**. The dirty Founder worktree was carried forward and
**preserved** (no reset, no clean, no stash, no `checkout -- .`, no force push). **No deploy. `.env` never read. No
credential activated. No live provider call.**

**Increment identity:** the FIRST implementation workstream of the current handoff — Priority 1–3 — merging what the
brief framed as two separate UI projects (Brain, Logistics map) into ONE canonical-propagation architecture, because
both are projections over the same domain objects.

**The defect this closes (measured, not inferred).** Both surfaces were already projections of canonical stores — the
Brain reads `demoStore`/`prospectStore`/registries/KB; the map reads shipments + POs through the canonical accessors —
so neither was a static JSON fixture. What was missing was **propagation**, in two halves:

1. **the mutations stayed silent.** 17 modules / **39 canonical array-write sites** and **30 in-place record mutations**
   (PO status, shipment status/stage, compliance doc status, case/ticket status, deduction status, work items,
   automation approvals, CRM tasks, filing stages, funding pipeline, grants, reconciliation) changed canonical state
   without announcing it;
2. **the projections never subscribed.** `MercentaBrain` built its graph with `useMemo(..., [])` — once per mount — and
   the logistics queries cached their reads with a 30 s staleTime and no invalidation.

Consequence: creating a PO, acknowledging it, filing an ASN, approving a document or resolving a case changed the
domain but **not the screen** until a reload. That is exactly "interactive static/simulated presentation", and it is now
fixed at the architecture level rather than in two screens.

### 1. COMPLETED / VERIFIED

- **ONE canonical change signal, owned once.** `src/lib/domain/canonicalSignal.ts` holds the counter, the listener list
  and the notifier (a version bump carrying no payload); `src/data/prospectStore.ts` imports and re-exports it, so all
  existing import paths work with exactly one implementation in the process.
- **EVERY canonical mutation now announces itself** — array writes and in-place record mutations, across the data layer
  and the domain modules (commerce lifecycle, helpdesk/cases, compliance verification, deductions, returns tracking,
  DHL domain, work layer, automation approvals, CRM tasks, company filings, funding pipeline, grants, reconciliation,
  event feed, acquisition/onboarding, BI lifecycle).
- **ONE subscriber keeps every canonical read in step.** `useCanonicalQuerySync()` (mounted in `App.tsx`) invalidates
  the query cache on each signal, so shipments, POs, deductions, products, compliance documents, contracts, cases,
  invoices, payments and the audit log all re-read the domain after a mutation — no per-component subscription.
- **The Brain is dynamic.** `MercentaBrain` and the brand relationship map re-project on the signal; a real domain
  change grows the graph (nodes AND edges) and the new record is a findable entity — with its provenance — without a
  reload. Drag/zoom/click were never the claim; this is.
- **The Logistics map is dynamic.** Raising a PO → acknowledging it → filing the ASN makes the new consignment appear
  on the map, in the list and in the inspector with its truth state, live, tenant-scoped. Simulation still runs through
  the SAME domain contracts the live path will use; nothing is a separate fake presentation model, and no carrier is
  invented (Freight Collect stays channel-arranged; Mercenta-arranged resolves through the canonical lane rule).
- **A permanent gate, both halves.** `npm run validate:canonical-propagation` asserts from SOURCE that one signal
  implementation exists and that **every** mutating function signals, that the app mounts the one sync subscriber, that
  both Brain projections depend on the signal and that the logistics surfaces are fed only from canonical accessors —
  and from RUNTIME that a real domain mutation MOVES both projections, that another tenant does not gain it, that an
  unknown tenant still fails closed, and that with no mutation the projection is unchanged.

> ### ROUTING ARCHITECTURE — what is now explicit
>
> - **EXCLUSIVE (XOR)** — exactly one route; REFUSES when none holds, when several hold (ambiguity), when a
>   condition cannot be evaluated (fail-closed), or when the gateway definition is malformed (undeclared
>   route / unrouted condition / duplicate route / contradictory condition). A refusal is **never** terminal.
> - **PARALLEL (AND)** — every branch evaluated independently; **a failing branch never erases a sibling's
>   success**; a branch whose sequential prerequisite is unmet does not run and says so.
> - **INCLUSIVE (OR)** — the selected subset is exactly the conditions that held: **never exactly-one and
>   never always-all**; a false condition marks its route `not_applicable` with the reason; nothing
>   applicable refuses.
> - **FAN-IN / JOIN** — declared completion (all / declared_subset / quorum / any), required vs optional
>   branches, a quorum that is **never invented**, and states `waiting` / `satisfied` / `failed` /
>   `blocked_human_review`. **Completion is never inferred from the initiating operation**, and timed-out or
>   human-review branches never count.
> - **SEQUENTIAL / EVENT-BASED / COMPENSATION** — a dependent route waits for a positively-satisfied
>   prerequisite; an undeclared event is refused and surfaced; a route with no declared compensation is
>   routed to human review rather than ignored.
> - **RETRY / ESCALATION / EXCEPTION / APPROVAL / TERMINAL** — carried by declared outcomes (`retryable`,
>   `timed_out`, `failed`, `human_review`) that map to declared dispositions (`retry`, `escalation`,
>   `exception`, `human_review`), and by the terminal flag, which is **false whenever a refusal, an
>   attention branch or an unsatisfied join exists**.
> - **IDEMPOTENCE** — the decision id and the idempotency key are deterministic functions of the gateway
>   inputs (`<workflowId>|<gatewayId>|<conditionDigest>`), so a repeated sweep, double-click, retry,
>   replayed callback or scheduler re-run is SUPPRESSED and reported: no second decision, no second audit
>   entry, no second event. `branchIsolationPreserved` and `completionInferredFromInitiator: false` are
>   recorded on every decision.
>

> ### BUGS FOUND AND FIXED IN-SESSION (each with the regression test that now pins it)
>
> 1. **False-positive contradiction refusal (blocking).** The structural analyser treated "two conditions
>    sharing one declared rule that disagree" as a contradiction. The commercial gate legitimately declares
>    ONE precedence rule evaluated per-route, so **every** commercial gate evaluation was refused. Fix: a
>    contradiction now means the SAME condition id declared twice with disagreeing outcomes, or two
>    conditions owning the SAME route under the SAME rule. New regression test: *"one shared rule evaluated
>    per-route is NOT a contradiction (no false positive)"*. This was caught by the validator, not by
>    inspection — which is the point of the validator.
> 2. **A refusal was reported as terminal completion.** `terminal` was derived from branch outcomes alone, so
>    a refused gateway (whose branches are all `skipped`) read as terminal. Fix: `terminal` is forced
>    `false` for every refusal. Pinned by the refusal assertion.
> 3. **A fixable gap escalated to human review.** With the original ladder order, missing required terms made
>    a downstream condition unevaluable, so a fixable gap routed to `human_review` instead of
>    `remediation`. Fix: the declared precedence is now **blocked → remediation → human review → ready**, and
>    the ladder distinguishes "unmet by the observed values" from "could not be evaluated" — which is what
>    makes `remediation` (supply the information) beat `human_review` (needs a business decision). Pinned by
>    the missing-terms, unevaluable-lead-time and pinned-ladder assertions.
> 4. **Evidence-hygiene defect in my own Matrix rows.** 13 rows were first written as `built_and_tested`
>    without an e2e reference, and several evidence strings put an annotation before the path, so
>    `verify-registry.mjs` flagged them. Fix: honest status `built`, and a declared normaliser that moves
>    annotations after the first real path (no word dropped). Result: **0 issues reference any Phase 2 row**.

> ## ✅ M13c PHASE C — LEGACY FALSE-SUBMISSION STATE FIXED AT THE ROOT (2026-09-15, session 3)
>
> **Checkpoint verified before any edit (read-only):** branch `redesign/foundation`,
> HEAD `883652d` (one commit past the directive's stated `f2a7434` — the §10/§31
> funding-pipeline commit), protected baseline `959b4d2` confirmed an ancestor,
> `git status --short` → **clean**. No repository-wide audit was performed; work
> started from this file and `HANDOFF.md`.
>
> **THE DEFECT:** `src/lib/grants/researchEngine.ts` wrote `status: 'submitted'`
> (`approveGrantDraft`) and `status: 'sent'` (`approveInvestorDraft`) onto its
> stored drafts with **no external submission occurring** and no approval gate —
> state that any surface could read as an external event Mercenta performed.
>
> **THE FIX** (uses the §31 `fundingPipeline` approval model as the architectural
> precedent — internal approval is a different thing from external submission):
> | Change | File |
> |---|---|
> | `GrantApplicationDraft.status` / `InvestorOutreachDraft.status` are now `'draft' \| 'approved_internally'`. The `submitted` and `sent` values **no longer exist**, so nothing can compile against them. | `src/types.ts` |
> | `submittedAt` / `submittedBy` / `sentAt` / `sentBy` renamed to `approvedAt` / `approvedBy` — an internal approval, not an external event. | `src/types.ts` |
> | `approveGrantDraft` / `approveInvestorDraft` record **INTERNAL approval only**, with the approver's identity, and are fail-closed: an approval that names nobody is refused. | `src/lib/grants/researchEngine.ts` |
> | A separate `submission` record plus `recordGrantSubmission` / `recordInvestorSubmission` is the **ONLY** path that can represent an external submission (the founder's own reference). Mirrors `recordFundingSubmission`: refused without explicit confirmation, without a prior internal approval, without a reference, or on a duplicate. | `src/lib/grants/researchEngine.ts` |
> | Declared facts `DRAFT_SUBMISSION_IS_A_FOUNDER_ACTION` + `DRAFT_INTERNAL_APPROVAL_DISCLAIMER` for the UI/validators. | `src/lib/grants/researchEngine.ts` |
> | 17 new deterministic checks appended to the **existing** validator (no duplicate validation infrastructure was created). | `scripts/validate-funding-pipeline.mjs` |
>
> **UI preserved (no redesign, no layout/styling change):** the drafts table
> renders the same way; the labels now derive from the renamed states
> (`internally approved — NOT submitted externally` / `— NOT sent externally`).
> The only visible copy changes are the two `Approve & Send` buttons and the one
> sentence naming that action — both stated "Send" for an action that sends
> nothing, so they now read **`Approve internally`**. Reported here rather than
> changed silently (the honesty rule this phase exists to enforce).
>

> ### 0A.3 PLATFORM INTEGRATION / DATA-FLOW MATRIX
> Edges judged: **exists?** (entities both exist) · **connected?** (data actually
> propagates) · **state propagated?** (state transitions flow) · **simulated
> correctly?** · **tested?** (validator/spec) · **E2E?** · **broken/missing?**
>
> **Flow 1 — Brand commercial chain (the core):**
> Brand → Product → ASIN → Amazon opportunity → PO → PO acknowledgement →
> Fulfilment → Shipment → Receiving → Invoice → Payment → Chargeback/Exception
> | Edge | exists | connected | propagated | sim correct | tested | E2E | broken/missing |
> |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
> | brand → product/catalog | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | — |
> | product → ASIN | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | PART (ASIN is BI-captured evidence; SP-API live CRED) |
> | ASIN → Amazon opportunity | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | — |
> | Amazon opportunity → PO | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | — |
> | PO → acknowledgement | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | — |
> | ack → fulfilment | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | — |
> | fulfilment → shipment/ASN | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | live labels CRED |
> | shipment → receiving | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | — |
> | receiving → invoice | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | — |
> | invoice → payment | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | LIVE Stripe CRED |
> | payment → chargeback/exception | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | — |
> | exception → dispute → case | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | — |
> **Verdict: the commercial chain is ONE connected deterministic lifecycle (proven by the 25-stage demo + E4 gates); no edge is missing; live lanes are CRED/F-ACTION only.**
>
> **Flow 2 — Acquisition chain:**
> Brand discovery → Brand Intelligence → Opportunity → ICP → Prospect → Contact →
> CRM → Outreach → Acquisition → Brand onboarding
> | Edge | exists | connected | propagated | sim correct | tested | E2E | broken/missing |
> |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
> | discovery → BI | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | — |
> | BI → Opportunity Discovery | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | — |
> | Opportunity → ICP | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | — |
> | ICP → Prospect | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | — |
> | Prospect → Contact | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Hunter live CRED |
> | Contact → CRM | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | — |
> | CRM → Outreach | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | live send CRED |
> | Outreach → Acquisition/response → Opportunity | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | — |
> | Acquisition → brand onboarding | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | — (E1/E2 hand-off) |
> **Verdict: acquisition is ONE connected flow (Phase C/D2/D4); durable persistence is memory-only in the demo (D4 schema unexecuted) — the only PART here.**

> **Flow 3 — Founder chain:**
> Opportunity → Funding/Investor → Founder approval → Application →
> Company/Government/Google support → Command Centre
> | Edge | exists | connected | propagated | sim correct | tested | E2E | broken/missing |
> |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
> | opportunity → funding/investor | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | — |
> | funding → founder approval gate | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | — |
> | approval → application record | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | — |

> | all → Command Centre rank+WHY+CTA | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | Y | — (tab-aware routing) |
> **Verdict: connected; no fabricated external submission anywhere (founder-gated).**

> | ID | Feature / Function | Req | Impl | Wired | Sim | Tested | E2E | Cred | F-Act | Def | Miss | Broke |
> |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
> | PA-01 | Dedicated Mercenta OpenRouter key (Super Admin in-memory entry; NEVER hardcoded; `VITE_OPENROUTER_API_KEY` env-hint only) | YES | YES | YES | CRED | YES | YES | CRED | NO | NO | NO | NO |
> | PA-02 | FREE models only — **BOTH runtime tasks have `freeModelSufficient: false` → resolve to paid `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` when a key is present** | YES | **PARTIAL** | **PARTIAL** | SIM-default | YES | YES | CRED | NO | NO | NO | **NO-code-defect-but-spec-conflict** |
> | PA-03 | No paid runtime model usage — **`MAX_PAID_RUNTIME_MODEL` IS a paid model; `isModelAllowed` permits it; £0.02/call budget is a ceiling, not a prohibition → VIOLATES agreed "FREE ONLY / NO PAID"** | YES | PARTIAL | PARTIAL | N/A | YES | YES | CRED | NO | NO | NO | **SPEC-CONFLICT — REQUIRES SPECIFICATION RECONCILIATION** (do not modify in 0B) |
> | PA-04 | No substitution of another/default OpenRouter key; no Cline model for runtime | YES | YES | YES | N/A | YES | YES | NO | NO | NO | NO | NO |
> | PA-05 | Deterministic-first (rules/business logic before any model; `RUNTIME_TASKS` declared) | YES | YES | YES | deterministic | YES | YES | NO | NO | NO | NO | NO |
> | PA-06 | Simulation/demo must not consume paid credits unnecessarily (call sites default to mock; real only behind key; usage log + ceilings) | YES | YES | YES | SIM | YES | YES | CRED | NO | NO | NO | NO |
> | PA-07 | Super Admin configurability of the key | YES | YES | YES | CRED | YES | YES | CRED | NO | NO | NO | NO |
>
> **Platform AI verdict (RECORD — DO NOT MODIFY):** dedicated-key rule,
> deterministic-first, config-safety and call-site gating all conform. But the
> **"FREE models only, no paid" rule is NOT met**: both declared runtime tasks
> resolve `paid_max` with a paid model when a key is supplied, `isModelAllowed`
> permits the paid max, and the per-op budget is a ceiling, not an absolute
> prohibition. Recorded as a **spec-vs-implementation conflict for Phase 1**
> (candidate: force `free_model` only, or obtain an explicit founder written
> exemption changing the agreed rule). Cline's own dev model was NOT changed.

> files — hence the rotation requirement below is not optional.

> ## ✅ §39 RLS FINDING — RESOLVED (M13) — 2026-09-14
>
> The M12 checkpoint flagged "shipping_margins / audit_log / leads /
> integration_connections have no ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY" and said it needed an
> owner decision. It was investigated properly instead of guessed at, and the
> conclusion differs from the checkpoint's wording in two ways:
>
> **1. Most of it was a stale VALIDATOR, not a stale schema.** `rls-audit.mjs`
> checked a hardcoded 13-table list and demanded `auth.uid()`. This schema's
> canonical tenancy predicate is `(auth.jwt() ->> 'tenant_id')::uuid`, so that check
> could NEVER pass — 23 "failures", almost all false negatives. It also named seven
> tables that **do not exist anywhere in the migration history** (grep → 0 hits):
> `shipping_margins`, `subscriptions`, `commissions`, `fulfillment_scores`,
> `ad_spend_budgets`, `leads`, `integration_connections` (and `compliance_documents`
> is really `compliance_docs`). There was no table, so there was no RLS gap.
> The audit is now **derived from the migrations themselves** (single source of
> truth) and audits **every** table: 33 tables, 33 RLS-enabled, 48 policies,
> **94 checks, 0 failures** (`RLS_STATIC_AUDIT_PASS`).
>
> **2. Two REAL gaps were hiding in that noise — both now fixed** by migration
> **027_harden_audit_log_rls.sql**:
> - **`audit_log` had NO RLS at all** (015 was created with the comment *"no RLS -
>   admin-only cross-tenant view"*). Admin-only in the UI is not a database control:
>   any role with a table grant could read every tenant's audit rows **and could
>   UPDATE or DELETE them**, destroying history. Now: RLS on, staff-only SELECT
>   (`auth.jwt() ->> 'role'`), authenticated append-only INSERT, and **no
>   update/delete policy at all** — the trail is immutable from the client;
>   service-role operations are unaffected. Also repairs a real persistence bug
>   found while reading the table: the three client insert paths write
>   `brand_id` / `reason` / `metadata`, which 015 never created, so those audit rows
>   were being silently dropped (`add column if not exists`).
> - **`applications` had NO RLS at all** (018). It holds applicant PII plus
>   `admin_notes` / `reviewed_by`, and with no policy a submitter could have
>   approved itself. Now: public INSERT that can only create `status = 'pending'`,
>   staff-only SELECT/UPDATE, no DELETE. This gap was invisible before because the
>   old hardcoded list never contained `applications` at all.
>
> **Tested:** `scripts/validate-rls-hardening.mjs` (NEW, 16 checks, PASS) pins both
> fixes so they cannot silently regress; `rls-audit.mjs` PASS (94 checks). Three
> stale migration-count assertions (E5 J1, E6 F4, E7 latest, `validate-db-hardening`)
> were repointed 026 → 027 with the invariant preserved and the repoint documented
> inline, and E6/E7's working-tree scope guards now declare the M13 surface
> explicitly instead of failing on an unexplained path.

## BI Forensic Implementation Audit (READ-ONLY, 2026-09-11)

> Status: **DONE (audit only — no product change)**. Report:
> `docs/BI_FORENSIC_IMPLEMENTATION_AUDIT_2026-09-11.md` (33 sections, 1630 lines).
> Scope: establish, from code + executed runtime evidence, exactly what Brand
> Intelligence does today. **No source, config, schema, test, prompt, provider,
> UI, navigation, lifecycle, ICP, acquisition, CRM or outreach file was
> modified; nothing was committed or deployed; no Phase D work started.**
>
> **Evidence executed in that session:** `npm run typecheck` → 0 errors ·
> `npm run build` → ✓ 2.29s · `validate-bi-lifecycle.mjs` → **PASS (29
> assertions, incl. "ZERO external network calls")** · `validate-prospect-pipeline.mjs`
> → **PASS (26/26)** · `validate-acquisition-pipeline.mjs` → **PASS** ·
> `npx playwright test e2e/brand-intelligence-lifecycle.spec.ts
> e2e/acquisition-pipeline.spec.ts` → **6 passed (19.2s), EXIT=0** · temporary
> Vite-SSR diagnostic (created, run, **deleted**) → `EXTERNAL FETCHES: 0`.
>
> **Headline findings (baseline facts, not recommendations):**
> 1. BI has **no live data source of any kind** (0 network calls; 12 hand-written
>    seed records; `createBrandIntelligenceClient()` always returns `MockClient`
>    and ignores its `_forceMock` argument).
> 2. No ASIN discovery, no product fetch, no sales estimation, no contact
>    discovery, no company enrichment: `discoveryClient.ts` is **dead code (0
>    callers)**; 14 ASINs are synthetic literals; 0 emails/phones/LinkedIn URLs
>    exist in the dataset.
> 3. The scoring engine **never applies `INTELLIGENCE_SCORE_WEIGHTS`** (dead
>    constant), sums raw sub-scores (max reachable **92**, not 100),
>    **double-counts the challenger bonus**, and derives `salesEstimateScore`
>    from the average rating.
> 4. The seed `score:` literals are **dead data**: the engine always recomputes
>    different values (Tapatío 75/tier_3 → **68/tier_4**); 8 of 12 brands fall
>    below the tier_4 floor, so `Lead.priority='High'` and the upper UI tiers are
>    unreachable.
> 5. Snapshots are written **per run** (not weekly as the type comment says),
>    are **empty at boot**, and are **never rendered**; `nextCheck` is a display
>    stamp with **no scheduler and no consumer**.
> 6. Persistence is **session-only in-memory**: no BI table/migration/Supabase
>    call/browser storage anywhere.
> 7. `VIEW_ALLOWLIST` / `canAccessView` / `filterNavForTier` in `rbac.ts` have

## 7D — Regression / skip-debt cleanup

**Commits:** `9666525` (product fixes + test-contract repairs) + this checkpoint commit.

**Baseline measured before edits (19-suite set, this session):** 79 passed / 1 failed (legal-agreements t1) / 48 skipped.

**Final result (same 19-suite set, after repair): 121 passed / 0 failed / 5 skipped.** All 5 remaining skips individually classified and justified below.

**Skip audit method:** re-ran every suite from scratch; for each of the 48 runtime skips inspected the actual `test.fixme` branch that fired, mapped it to the CURRENT UI contract (nav routing after Phase 6, renamed views/labels, moved data surfaces), then applied the smallest safe repair — fixing the test contract OR the small product defect that caused it. No assertions weakened, no conditional-on-failure logic, no DOM faking, no app-state injection.

**Product defects found and fixed (small, clearly intended):**
1. **`TourEngine` per-view auto-start was only wired for the PO tour** — `autoStartViews` on the other 8 tours were inert. Now the generic reg: any tour declaring `autoStartViews` starts on that brand view (catalog → Tour 2, analytics → Tour 5, logistics → Tour 4, compliance → Tour 6, settings → Tour 9/7, team → Tour 8). Fix: `src/components/shared/TourEngine.tsx` (loops `ALL_TOUR_DEFINITIONS`).
2. **Dispute writes hung in demo mode** — the async `disputeDeduction`/`recordDisputeOutcome` awaited the Supabase write BEFORE applying the in-memory store mutation, so with an unreachable host the demo store never updated (row never became disputed/resolved; audit never written). Fix: `src/data/api.ts` — apply the local store mutation first, background the DB write. Also `queryOrSeed` now returns a fresh `slice()` so React Query observers see a new reference after invalidation and re-render (previously identical identity = stale UI).
3. **Admin CRM Override with an empty reason silently threw** (`setBrandTrack` requires a reason) — no UI feedback. Fix: `BrandCRM.tsx` surfaces “Override reason is required…” instead of throwing.
4. **Brand logistics feed used only the mounted dossier snapshot** (stale, never reflected new drafts/ASN shipments). Fix: `LogisticsHub.tsx` reads the live `useShipmentsAll` feed, tenant-scoped for brand sessions; `BrandPurchaseOrders.tsx` invalidates the shipments query on ack/ASN so auto-created drafts and filed shipments appear immediately.
5. **Homepage Publish in demo mode could never surface on the public page** — `fetchHomepageContent` always returned `DEFAULT_HOMEPAGE_CONTENT` as “live”. Fix: session live-copy (`homepageState.live`) set on publish, returned by fetch in demo mode (Supabase path unchanged).

**Documented product gaps (deferred — NOT implemented in 7D):**
- Tour restart control from Brand Settings does not exist (tours t7 stays skipped with reason; small Settings feature → later phase).
- Tour 5 (Deductions on Analytics) starts, but its tour target attributes (e.g. `data-tour="deductions-benefits"`) do not exist in the SalesAnalytics surface — card cannot render its highlight (tours t5 stays skipped; data-tour rotation belongs to the later data-tour sweep).
  - **→ CLOSED in Phase G1 (2026-09-13):** the four Tour-5 targets now exist on the brand deductions ledger, mounted on Analytics **and** Reports; `tours` t5 is no longer skipped — it is a genuine passing functional + tenant-isolation test.
- Demo-mode post-publish home view does not auto-refresh the already-mounted public homepage (persistence/refresh work → later phase).
- Dispute resolution writes to the store + audit, but the live ledger row refresh relies on the React Query reference fix; the visual “→ outcome: partial” badge path is covered by the same mechanism and verified for won/lost seed rows.
- Not-representable data states (portal tenants are all compliance-cleared; no pending profile-change requests seed): these remain conditional skips because inventing demo data/state to drive them would violate the no-fake-state rule.

**Remaining skipped tests (all justified):**
- compliance-gate t1 `0/5 → blocked` — ENV/DATA state: no portal tenant with 0 approved docs; retained.
- compliance-gate t2 `4/5 → still blocked` — same; retained.
- crm t3 `profile-change review UI` — seed has no pending requests; the review UI is verified when pending; retained as data-conditional.
- tours t5 `Deductions tour on Analytics` — selectors do not exist yet; retained (deferred data-tour work).
- tours t7 `Settings has tour restart` — feature not built; retained (deferred feature).

**Previously-passing regression check:** the 79 tests passing at baseline still pass in the final run (no title-collision regressions; the renamed tests are the same contracts under corrected names). 0 unexplained new failures.

### Compliance-state architecture
- Compliance business logic UNCHANGED and canonical (`src/lib/compliance.ts` — docs + contract + §4.1/§4.2 agreement inputs). No second engine, no test-only branch, no bypassed onboarding.
- `portal access` and `gate clearance` are now decoupled via two new canonical registries in `src/data/demoData.ts`:
  - `CLEARED_BRAND_IDS` — cleared tenants (unchanged: Zambezi, DeskForge).
  - `COMPLIANCE_SCENARIO_BRAND_IDS` — portal tenants that are NOT gate-cleared.
  - `PORTAL_BRAND_IDS` = cleared + scenario (drives `onboarded` in `brandDossiers.ts`).
  - `COMPLIANCE_SCENARIO_DOC_STATES` — explicit per-required-type statuses that OVERRIDE the rotating pattern for scenario tenants (see matrix).

### Deterministic compliance test states

## 7B — Defect repair + regression stabilization

Executed 2026-09-09 in the mandated order A→F. Branch `redesign/foundation`; protected baseline `959b4d2` + tag `mercenta-baseline-before-redesign-20260907` intact.

### Repair A — GlobalStateContext bootstrap defect (confirmed runtime crash)
- **Cause:** `const [campaigns] = useState<Campaign[]>([]);` (no setter) while the lazy-bootstrap `useEffect` calls `setCampaigns(m.INITIAL_CAMPAIGNS)` → `ReferenceError: setCampaigns is not defined` on EVERY app mount (real browser repro).
- **Fix:** restored the setter — `const [campaigns, setCampaigns] = useState<Campaign[]>([]);`. Nothing else in the bootstrap sequence / campaigns / apiLogs / staff behavior touched.
- **Verified:** pageerror gone in browser; Zambesi/DeskForge portals render; no new runtime exception.

### Repair B — ComplianceHub argument shift (confirmed)
- **Cause:** `evaluateComplianceGate(brandDocs, hasSignedAgreement)` put the boolean into the `category` parameter (canonical signature `(docs, category?, hasSignedAgreement=false, …)`).
- **Fix:** minimal call-site change → `evaluateComplianceGate(brandDocs, undefined, hasSignedAgreement)`.
- **Verified:** compliance-gate suite green in its representable states; catalog CTA for a cleared tenant is enabled (correct agreement state in browser).

### Repair C — Brand Purchase Orders runtime crash (root cause traced)
- **Root cause:** `BrandShell` renders `TourLoader`, `UsertourBrandBridge`, and `BrandCommPanel` (all call `useIntegrations()`) inside its ErrorBoundary WITHOUT a provider — unlike `AdminShell`; `main.tsx`/`App.tsx` provide none globally → every onboarded brand view crashed into "Brand portal — something went wrong" (`useIntegrations must be used within IntegrationsProvider`). Reproduced in a real browser; the defect predates Phase 6 (same structure at `e7fa882^`).
- **Fix (smallest justified):** wrap BrandShell content in `<IntegrationsProvider>` mirroring AdminShell exactly.
- **Verified:** Zambezi → Purchase Orders renders PO-9000/PO-9001; ErrorBoundary message gone in browser; multi-tenant suite green.

### Repair D — ESLint hooks enforcement
- **Config:** `react-hooks/rules-of-hooks` + `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` restored to `error` (were `'off'`, contradicting the §Stage-18 documentation that they must FAIL).
- **Genuine Rules-of-Hooks defects fixed (≤3 files):** `RoutingRequest.tsx` — two `useMemo` calls were gated behind early returns (crash risk when the branch flips); hoisted above the guards.
- **Authorized syntax repairs (Section 13):** `XeroConnection.tsx` — stray `</div>` after the component + one missing `</div>` before `</Card>` (unclosed JSX, pre-baseline); `outreachGenerator.ts` — unescaped apostrophes in two single-quoted strings (`we'd`/`we've`), an empty `distNote` body restored, and an orphaned `distributorsNote` helper body given its missing function header (all pre-baseline corruption).
- **Result:** lint 41 → 37 problems; repaired files lint/tsc-clean. The 30 remaining `exhaustive-deps` errors span 13 files (logical-expression-as-dep patterns) + 7 legacy style errors (no-var/prefer-const) — all pre-existing patterns and beyond the 5-file per-repair scope → reported, not silently edited (separate approved workstream required).

### Repair E — Phase 6 tour-attribute regression
- **Cause:** the Phase 6 grouped-nav regroup dropped `tourAttr` from nav items (`Sidebar` still renders `data-tour={item.tourAttr}`); canonical identifiers recovered from the original `src/App.tsx` BRAND_NAV (commit 69a3473).
- **Fix:** restored `tourAttr` on the six tour-targeted brand nav items (`brand-dashboard`, `nav-catalog`, `nav-purchase_orders`, `nav-logistics`, `nav-compliance`, `nav-settings`) in `BrandShell.tsx` BRAND_SECTIONS. Also fixed a pre-existing `TourEngine` defect the tour tests exposed: the last-step tooltip rendered outside the 720px viewport (completion button unclickable) — added a vertical viewport clamp (positioning fix, not a redesign/sequencing change).
- **Verified (browser):** all 6 `data-tour` attributes PRESENT for an onboarded tenant; Tour 1 auto-starts; tours.spec **6 passed / 3 skipped** (was 1 pass/3 fail/5 skip). The 3 skips are honest `fixme` (Tour 2/5 per-view auto-start not wired in TourEngine; Settings restart option not present) — recorded.
